hook_text: An exam hands you a photo of a town from straight above. Where is the CBD? Prove it.
clip_script: Start with north, the scale and the big features: river, railway, main roads. Where the main road crosses the railway, buildings are tallest and tightest, with long shadows: that is the CBD. Big roofs, round tanks, a railway line running straight into the site: industry. Big plots, trees, little blue squares that are swimming pools, curved streets: a high-income suburb. Long tight rows of small houses beyond the railway: a low-income area, separated by a buffer. A strip of green along the river: parks on the flood plain. Then measure: on one to ten thousand, one centimetre is one hundred metres. Claim, evidence, explanation.
visual_style: A whiteboard vertical view of a small town with a river and railway, zones appearing one at a time with arrows pointing to the clues.
pacing: Zone by zone, steady, with a punchy ending.
